title.raw: 卷一百二十七 載記第二十七 慕容德 Volume 12 Records 27: Murong De

sentences.zh: 慕容德

translations.literal: Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De.

sentences.zh: 慕容德，字玄明，皝之少子也，母公孫氏夢日入臍中，晝寢而生德。

translations.literal: Murong De, courtesy name Xuanming, was the youngest son of Huang; his mother Lady Gongsun dreamed the sun entered her navel and, sleeping by day, gave birth to De.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De, whose courtesy name was Xuanming, was Murong Huang’s youngest son. His mother Lady Gongsun dreamed of the sun slipping into her navel, then bore him in a daytime doze.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，身長八尺二寸，姿貌雄偉，額有日角偃月重文。

translations.literal: Before the weak-crown age he was eight chi two cun in height, his bearing majestic, his forehead having double markings of sun-corner and reclining moon.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he already stood eight feet two inches tall, cut an imposing figure, and bore the paired “sun-brow” and “crescent moon” lines on his forehead that physiognomists read as imperial signs.

sentences.zh: 博觀群書，性清慎，多才藝。

translations.literal: He broadly perused many books; his nature was clear and cautious; he had many talents and arts.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely, kept a cool and careful temper, and excelled at more than one craft.

sentences.zh: 慕容俊之僭立也，封為梁公，曆幽州刺史、左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Murong Jun presumptuously established himself, he was enfeoffed Duke of Liang, and served as inspector of You Province and left guard general.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Jun declared himself emperor, Murong De was made duke of Liang and rose through posts as inspector of You and general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 及垂嗣位，改范陽王，稍遷魏尹，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Chui succeeded the throne, he was changed to Prince of Fanyang, gradually promoted prefect of Wei, with addition of regular attendant for scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui took the throne Murong De was refashioned prince of Fanyang, then advanced to prefect of the Wei capital region and given the concurrent title of regular attendant for scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 俄而苻堅將苻雙據陝以叛，堅將苻柳起兵枹罕，將應之。

translations.literal: Soon Fu Jian’s general Fu Shuang seized Shan and rebelled; Jian’s general Fu Liu raised troops at Baohan to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fu Shuang, one of Fu Jian’s generals, rebelled from Shan commandery, while another general, Fu Liu, rose at Baohan to join him.

sentences.zh: 德勸垂乘釁討堅，辭旨慷慨，識者言其有遠略，垂竟不能用。

translations.literal: De urged Chui to exploit the opening to punish Jian; his words were fervent; observers said he had long-range strategy; Chui in the end could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De urged Murong Chui to strike Fu Jian while Qin was divided, speaking with such fire that men of judgment called him far-sighted—yet Murong Chui would not act.

sentences.zh: 德兄垂甚壯之，因共論軍國大謀，言必切至。

translations.literal: De’s elder brother Chui greatly admired him; therefore they together discussed great plans of army and state; his words were always incisive and to the point.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui, impressed, began debating statecraft and strategy with him, and Murong De’s advice was always blunt and to the point.

sentences.zh: 垂謂之曰：「汝器識長進，非復吳下阿蒙也。

translations.literal: Chui said to him: “Your capacity and insight have advanced; you are no longer the young Meng east of Wu.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui told him, “Your judgment has matured—you are no longer the raw boy they used to dismiss east of the Yangzi.”

sentences.zh: 」枋頭之役，德以征南將軍與垂擊敗晉師。

translations.literal: In the Fangtou campaign, De as general who campaigns south together with Chui struck and defeated Jin troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Fangtou he joined Murong Chui as general who campaigns south and helped shatter the Eastern Jin army.

sentences.zh: 及垂奔苻堅，德坐免職。

translations.literal: When Chui fled to Fu Jian, De sat fault and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui defected to Fu Jian, Murong De lost his post as an accomplice.

sentences.zh: 後遇垂敗，徙于長安，苻堅以為張掖太守，數歲免歸。

translations.literal: Later encountering Chui’s defeat, he was moved to Chang’an; Fu Jian appointed him prefect of Zhangye; after several years he was dismissed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Chui’s rebellion collapsed he was deported to Chang’an, where Fu Jian named him prefect of Zhangye; a few years later he was sent home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 及堅以兵臨江，拜德為奮威將軍。

translations.literal: When Jian led troops to the Yangzi, he appointed De general who rouses might.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian marched his host to the great river, he named Murong De general who rouses might.

sentences.zh: 堅之敗也，堅與張夫人相失，慕容垂將護致之，德正色謂垂曰：「昔楚莊滅陳，納巫臣之諫而棄夏姬。

translations.literal: When Jian was defeated, Jian and Lady Zhang the consort lost each other; Murong Chui was about to escort and bring her; De with stern countenance said to Chui: “In the past when King Zhuang of Chu destroyed Chen, he accepted Wu Chen’s remonstrance and cast aside Xia Ji.
translations.idiomatic: After Feishui, Fu Jian was separated from Lady Zhang. Murong Chui meant to rescue her and bring her along. Murong De said gravely, “When King Zhuang of Chu annexed Chen he listened to Wu Chen and turned his back on the fatal beauty Xia Ji.

sentences.zh: 此不祥之人，惑亂人主，戎事不邇女器，秦之敗師當由於此。

translations.literal: This is an unlucky person who deludes and disorders the ruler; in military affairs one does not draw near women’s vessels; Qin’s defeated army ought to have come from this.
translations.idiomatic: Such women are ill omens—they topple kings. Camp followers and concubines have no place in a retreating army; Qin’s rout began with just this sort of indulgence.”

sentences.zh: 宜掩目而過，奈何將衛之也！

translations.literal: One ought to cover the eyes and pass by—how can you intend to escort and guard her!
translations.idiomatic: Cover your eyes and ride past—why would you drag her into our column?”

sentences.zh: 」垂不從，德馳馬而去之。

translations.literal: Chui did not follow; De galloped horse and left him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui refused to listen; Murong De spurred his horse and rode away in disgust.

sentences.zh: 還次滎陽，言於垂曰：「昔句踐棲於會稽，終獲吳國。

translations.literal: Returning he halted at Xingyang and said to Chui: “In the past Goujian lodged at Kuaiji and in the end obtained Wu state.
translations.idiomatic: When they halted at Xingyang he told Murong Chui, “Goujian of Yue once swallowed humiliation on Mount Kuaiji—and in the end swallowed Wu.”

sentences.zh: 聖人相時而動，百舉百全。

translations.literal: Sages observe the times and move; a hundred undertakings, a hundred completions.
translations.idiomatic: The sage waits for the moment; when he moves, every stroke succeeds.”

sentences.zh: 天將悔禍，故使秦師喪敗，宜乘其弊以復社稷。

translations.literal: Heaven will repent the calamity; therefore it caused Qin army to lose and be defeated; one ought to ride their exhaustion to restore altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is already punishing Qin for its crimes—its hosts lie broken on the field. Strike now while they reel and you can win back the Murong altars.”

sentences.zh: 」垂不納。

translations.literal: Chui did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui would not listen.

sentences.zh: 乃從垂如鄴。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed Chui to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De followed him north to Ye.

sentences.zh: 及垂稱燕王，以德為車騎大將軍，復封范陽王，居中鎮衛，參斷政事。

translations.literal: When Chui styled himself King of Yan, he appointed De chariot-and-cavalry grand general, again enfeoffed Prince of Fanyang, stayed within to guard and defend, and joined in deciding government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui declared himself king of Yan he made Murong De grand general of chariots and cavalry, restored his princedom of Fanyang, kept him at court to secure the capital, and gave him a voice in every policy decision.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷司徙。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred Minister of Education (司徙).
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to minister of education.

sentences.zh: 于時慕容永據長子，有眾十萬，垂議討之。

translations.literal: At that time Murong Yong held Changzi and had a host of one hundred thousand, and Murong Chui deliberated attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Murong Yong held Changzi with a hundred thousand men under arms, and Murong Chui planned a campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 群臣咸以為疑，德進曰：「昔三祖積德，遺詠在耳，故陛下龍飛，不謀而會，雖由聖武，亦緣舊愛，燕、趙之士樂為燕臣也。

translations.literal: The ministers all harbored doubts, and Murong De stepped forward and said that in olden days the three ancestors had piled up virtue and their lingering praise was still in the ears, so His Majesty's dragon ascent had brought men together without prior plotting; though this owed to sacred martial prowess, it was also due to old affection, and the gentry of Yan and Zhao were glad to be subjects of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers hesitated, but Murong De came forward and argued that the three royal forebears had long accumulated moral credit still remembered in song, which was why Murong Chui's rise had drawn support as if by fate; while his martial prestige mattered, old loyalty mattered too, and the elite of Yan and Zhao were willing to serve Later Yan.

sentences.zh: 今永既建偽號，扇動華戎，致令群豎從橫，逐鹿不息，宜先除之，以一眾聽。

translations.literal: Now Yong had already assumed a false title, stirred Chinese and non-Chinese, and made petty rivals roam unchecked while the struggle for supremacy never ceased, so he ought to be removed first in order to unify what the multitude listened to.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Murong Yong had proclaimed an illegitimate regime, incited Chinese and frontier peoples, and set petty warlords loose in endless rivalry for the realm, Murong Yong should be eliminated first to align the army's will.

sentences.zh: 昔光武馳蘇茂之難，不顧百官之疲，夫豈不仁？

translations.literal: Formerly Guangwu pressed through the crisis of Su Mao and did not heed the weariness of the hundred officials; was that not unkind?
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Guangwu had rushed into Su Mao's crisis without sparing his weary officials; that was hardly cruelty on his part.

sentences.zh: 機急故也。

translations.literal: The opportunity was urgent; that was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The circumstances were desperate, and that explained it.

sentences.zh: 兵法有不得已而用之，陛下容得已乎！

translations.literal: The art of war admits using force when one cannot do otherwise; could His Majesty possibly do otherwise?
translations.idiomatic: Military doctrine allows action when there is no alternative; Murong Chui could hardly afford to stand aside.

sentences.zh: 」垂笑謂其黨曰：「司徒議與吾同。

translations.literal: Murong Chui smiled and told his followers that the Minister of Education's view matched his own.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui smiled and told his faction that the minister of education's counsel aligned with his own.

sentences.zh: 二人同心，其利斷金，吾計決矣。

translations.literal: When two share one mind, their edge can sever metal; his plan was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Two minds in accord can cut through bronze, he said, and his decision was made.

sentences.zh: 」遂從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Murong Chui followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 垂臨終，敕其子寶以鄴城委德。

translations.literal: As Murong Chui neared death, he instructed his son Murong Bao to entrust Ye to Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Murong Chui ordered Murong Bao to place Ye in Murong De's hands.

sentences.zh: 寶既嗣位，以德為使持節、都督冀、兗、青、徐、荊、豫六州諸軍事、特進、車騎大將軍、冀州牧，領南蠻校尉，鎮鄴，罷留台，以都督專總南夏。

translations.literal: After Murong Bao succeeded, he appointed Murong De as commissioner bearing credentials, area commander-in-chief of military affairs in six provinces Ji, Yan, Qing, Xu, Jing, and Yu, specially advanced, chariot and cavalry general-in-chief, governor of Ji, concurrently colonel of the Southern Man, stationed at Ye, abolished the rear headquarters, and used the area command to oversee the southern summer in full.
translations.idiomatic: Once Murong Bao had taken the throne, he named Murong De commissioner with credentials, supreme commander over military affairs in Ji, Yan, Qing, Xu, Jing, and Yu, specially advanced, chariot-and-cavalry general-in-chief, and governor of Ji, with the southern barbarian colonelcy, based at Ye; he dissolved the rear administration and concentrated southern affairs under Murong De's unified command.

sentences.zh: 魏將拓拔章攻鄴，德遣南安王慕容青等夜擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Wei general Tuoba Zhang attacked Ye, and Murong De sent Murong Qing, Prince of Nan'an, and others to strike by night and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei commander Tuoba Zhang assaulted Ye, and Murong De dispatched Murong Qing, Prince of Nan'an, and others on a night attack that routed him.

sentences.zh: 魏師退次新城，青等請擊之。

translations.literal: The Wei army withdrew and halted at Xincheng, and Murong Qing and others requested to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei forces pulled back to Xincheng, where Murong Qing and his colleagues asked permission to attack.

sentences.zh: 別駕韓𧨳進曰：「古人先決勝廟堂，然後攻戰。

translations.literal: Adjutant Han Fan advanced and said that the ancients first secured victory in the council hall and afterward fought.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan, the provincial adjutant, urged that the ancients decided victory in council before they took the field.

sentences.zh: 今魏不可擊者四，燕不宜動者三。

translations.literal: Now there were four reasons Wei could not be attacked and three reasons Yan ought not to move.
translations.idiomatic: He listed four reasons not to strike the Wei army and three reasons Later Yan should stay put.

sentences.zh: 魏懸軍遠入，利在野戰，一不可擊也。

translations.literal: Wei had hung an army far from home and profited from field battle, so the first was that they could not be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's troops were deep in hostile territory and favored open battle, which was the first reason not to engage them.

sentences.zh: 深入近畿，頓兵死地，二不可擊也。

translations.literal: They had penetrated near the capital region and halted their troops on deadly ground, so the second was that they could not be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: They had thrust close to the heartland and camped on perilous ground, which was the second reason to hold off.

sentences.zh: 前鋒既敗，後陣方固，三不可擊也。

translations.literal: The vanguard had already been defeated while the rear ranks were just firming up, so the third was that they could not be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Their front had been beaten but their rear was consolidating, which was the third reason to avoid battle.

sentences.zh: 彼眾我寡，四不可擊也。

translations.literal: The enemy were many and Murong De's side few, so the fourth was that they could not be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: They outnumbered Murong De's forces, which was the fourth reason not to strike.

sentences.zh: 官軍自戰其地，一不宜動。

translations.literal: The government army fought on its own ground, so the first was that it was not fitting to move.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De's army fought on home soil, which was the first reason not to stir.

sentences.zh: 動而不勝，眾心難固，二不宜動。

translations.literal: If they moved and did not win, the host's hearts would be hard to steady, so the second was that it was not fitting to move.
translations.idiomatic: A failed sortie would shatter morale, which was the second reason to stay still.

sentences.zh: 城郭未修，敵來無備，三不宜動。

translations.literal: The walls and moats were not yet repaired, so if the enemy came there was no readiness, and the third was that it was not fitting to move.
translations.idiomatic: The defenses were unfinished and left Murong De exposed if the enemy came, which was the third reason to remain passive.

sentences.zh: 此皆兵家所忌，不如深溝高壘，以逸待勞。

translations.literal: These were all things military strategists dreaded, and it was better to dig deep moats and raise high ramparts and await exhaustion with ease.
translations.idiomatic: These were classic taboos in the art of war; better to deepen ditches, heighten walls, and wait out the enemy at leisure.

sentences.zh: 彼千里饋糧，野無所掠，久則三軍靡資，攻則眾旅多斃，師老釁生，詳而圖之，可以捷矣。

translations.literal: They would haul grain a thousand li while the wilderness offered nothing to plunder, and in time the three armies would lack supplies; if they attacked, many companies would perish, the army would age and openings would appear, and if Murong De studied the situation he could win.
translations.idiomatic: Their supply lines stretched a thousand li across empty country, so prolonged operations would drain their stores; repeated assaults would bleed their columns, wear would breed disorder, and careful timing could bring victory.

sentences.zh: 」德曰：「韓別駕之言，良、平之策也。

translations.literal: Murong De said that Adjutant Han Fan's words were a strategy worthy of Liang and Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De replied that Han Fan's counsel matched the quality of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping.

sentences.zh: 」於是召青還師。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Murong Qing to return the army.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore recalled Murong Qing and withdrew the troops.

sentences.zh: 魏又遣遼西公賀賴盧率騎與章圍鄴，德遣其參軍劉藻請救于姚興，且參母兄之問，而興師不至，眾大懼。

translations.literal: Wei again sent Prince of Liaoxi Helai Lu leading cavalry to join Tuoba Zhang in besieging Ye, and Murong De sent his staff adviser Liu Zao to beg rescue from Yao Xing and also to inquire after Murong De's mother and elder brother, but Yao Xing's army did not arrive and the host was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Wei dispatched Helai Lu, Prince of Liaoxi, with cavalry to cooperate with Tuoba Zhang in the siege of Ye; Murong De sent Liu Zao to Yao Xing for aid and news of his mother and brother, but no relief came and panic spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 德於是親饗戰士，厚加撫接，人感其恩，皆樂為致死。

translations.literal: Murong De then personally feasted the fighters, treated them generously and comforted them, and men were moved by his kindness and all were glad to die for him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De then hosted the soldiers himself, lavished care on them, and they repaid his kindness with a will to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 會章、盧內相乖爭，各引軍潛遁。

translations.literal: It happened that Tuoba Zhang and Helai Lu quarreled within their ranks and each secretly led his army away.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Zhang and Helai Lu fell into mutual discord and slipped away with their commands.

sentences.zh: 章司馬丁建率眾來降，言章師老，可以敗之。

translations.literal: Tuoba Zhang's chief clerk Ding Tong led his masses to surrender and said Tuoba Zhang's army was worn and could be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Tong, chief clerk under Tuoba Zhang, defected with his troops and reported that Zhang's army was exhausted and vulnerable.

sentences.zh: 德遣將追破章軍，人心始固。

translations.literal: Murong De sent a general in pursuit and broke Tuoba Zhang's army, and only then did hearts begin to steady.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De sent a commander in pursuit who crushed Tuoba Zhang's force, and morale finally firmed.

sentences.zh: 時魏師入中山，慕容寶出奔于薊，慕容詳又僭號。

translations.literal: At that time Wei's army entered Zhongshan, Murong Bao fled toward Ji, and Murong Xiang again assumed an illegitimate title.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wei troops entered Zhongshan, Murong Bao fled toward Ji, and Murong Xiang proclaimed himself at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 會劉藻自姚興而至，興太史令高魯遣其甥王景暉隨藻送玉璽一紐，並圖識秘文，曰：「有德者昌，無德者亡。

translations.literal: It happened that Liu Zao returned from Yao Xing, and Yao Xing's grand astrologer Gao Lu sent his nephew Wang Jinghui with Liu Zao to deliver one jade seal and charts and esoteric prophetic texts saying that those with virtue flourished and those without perished.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zao came back from Yao Xing's court, Yao Xing's director of astronomy Gao Lu sent his nephew Wang Jinghui with him bearing a jade seal plus charts and cryptic prophecies declaring that virtue brought prosperity and its absence brought ruin.

sentences.zh: 德受天命，柔而復剛。

translations.literal: Murong De received Heaven's mandate, soft yet again hard.
translations.idiomatic: They proclaimed that Murong De bore Heaven's mandate, supple yet ultimately unyielding.

sentences.zh: 」又有謠曰：「大風蓬勃揚塵埃，八井三刀卒起來，四海鼎沸中山頹，惟有德人據三台。

translations.literal: There was also a rhyme saying that a great wind suddenly raised dust, eight wells and three blades would suddenly rise, the four seas seethed like a cauldron and Zhongshan fell, and only the man of virtue would occupy the Three Terraces.
translations.idiomatic: A popular verse added that whirlwinds would scour the land, cryptic signs would spark uprising, the realm would boil while Zhongshan collapsed, and only the virtuous man would seize the Three Terraces.

sentences.zh: 」於是德之群臣議以慕容詳僭號中山，魏師盛于冀州，未審寶之存亡，因勸德即尊號。

translations.literal: Thereupon Murong De's ministers deliberated because Murong Xiang had usurped the title at Zhongshan, Wei's army was strong in Ji province, and Murong Bao's life or death was unknown, and they therefore urged Murong De to assume the supreme honor.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De's officials argued that with Murong Xiang's usurpation at Zhongshan, Wei's power swelling in Ji, and Murong Bao's fate uncertain, Murong De should take the imperial dignity.

sentences.zh: 德不從。

translations.literal: Murong De did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De refused.

sentences.zh: 會慕容達自龍城奔鄴，稱寶猶存，群議乃止。

translations.literal: It happened that Murong Da fled from Longcheng to Ye and declared that Murong Bao still lived, and the collective deliberation then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Murong Da arrived from Longcheng claiming Murong Bao was alive, and the push for enthronement stopped.

sentences.zh: 尋而寶以德為丞相，領冀州牧，承制南夏。

translations.literal: Before long Murong Bao made Murong De chancellor and governor of Ji, with delegated authority over the southern summer.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao then appointed Murong De chancellor and governor of Ji, empowering him to govern the south.

sentences.zh: 德兄子麟自義台奔鄴，因說德曰：「中山既沒，魏必乘勝攻鄴，雖糧儲素積，而城大難固，且人情沮動，不可以戰。

translations.literal: Murong De's nephew Murong Lin fled from Yitai to Ye and therefore urged Murong De that since Zhongshan had fallen Wei would surely exploit victory to attack Ye; though grain had long been stored, the city was large and hard to defend, and moreover human hearts were shaken and battle was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin, Murong De's nephew, fled from Yitai to Ye and warned that Wei would press its victory against Ye after Zhongshan's fall; grain reserves were ample but the sprawling walls were hard to hold, and shaken morale made fighting unwise.

sentences.zh: 及魏軍未至，擁眾南渡，就魯陽王和，據滑台而聚兵積穀，伺隙而動，計之上也。

translations.literal: Before Wei's army arrived, Murong De should gather the host and cross south to join Prince of Luyang Murong He, occupy Huatai to mass troops and pile grain, and watch for an opening to move, which was the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Murong De to move the army south across the river before Wei arrived, join Murong He, Prince of Luyang, seize Huatai to stockpile men and supplies, and strike when opportunity allowed—the best course.

sentences.zh: 魏雖拔中山，勢不久留，不過驅掠而返。

translations.literal: Even if Wei took Zhongshan, its momentum would not long remain, and it would do no more than drive people off in plunder and return.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Wei seized Zhongshan, it could not linger; it would raid the population and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 人不樂徙，理自生變，然後振威以援之，魏則內外受敵，使戀舊之士有所依憑，廣開恩信，招集遺黎，可一舉而取之。

translations.literal: People would not relish removal, and by principle change would arise of itself, and afterward Murong De could shake his might to aid them so that Wei would suffer enemies within and without, let men who clung to their old homes have something to rely on, broadly open grace and trust, and summon the scattered commoners, and then Murong De could take them in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: The populace would resist forced migration and turmoil would follow; Murong De could then project power to support them, leaving Wei caught between interior and exterior foes, while he won over the displaced with mercy and credibility and gathered the refugees for a decisive blow.

sentences.zh: 」先是，慕容和亦勸德南徙，於是許之。

translations.literal: Earlier Murong He had also urged Murong De to move south, and Murong De therefore assented.
translations.idiomatic: Murong He had already advocated a southern shift, so Murong De agreed.

sentences.zh: 隆安二年，乃率戶四萬、車二萬七千乘，自鄴將徙於滑台。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longan Murong De then led forty thousand households and twenty-seven thousand carts and from Ye was about to relocate to Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: In Longan 2 Murong De moved forty thousand households and twenty-seven thousand carts from Ye toward Huatai.

sentences.zh: 遇風，船沒，魏軍垂至，眾懼，議欲退保黎陽。

translations.literal: Murong De met wind, the boats sank, Wei's army was almost upon them, the host was afraid, and they deliberated wishing to fall back and defend Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Storms sank the flotilla as Wei closed in, spreading panic and talk of retreating to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 其夕流澌凍合，是夜濟師，旦，魏師至而冰泮，若有神焉。

translations.literal: That evening floating ice froze solid, and that night Murong De's force crossed; at dawn Wei's army arrived as the ice broke up, as if there were spirits.
translations.idiomatic: That night the river froze solid, allowing a night crossing; by morning Wei arrived as the ice thawed, as though the gods favored Murong De.

sentences.zh: 遂改黎陽津為天橋津。

translations.literal: Murong De therefore changed the name of the Liyang ford to Tianqiao Ford.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed the Liyang crossing the Heavenly Bridge Ford.

sentences.zh: 及至滑台，景星見於尾箕。

translations.literal: When Murong De reached Huatai, an auspicious star appeared in the Tail and Winnow-basket asterisms.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Huatai, a propitious star appeared in the Tail and Basket lunar mansions.

sentences.zh: 漳水得白玉，狀若璽。

translations.literal: The Zhang River yielded white jade shaped like a seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang River produced white jade in the form of an imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 於是德依燕元故事，稱元年，大赦境內殊死已下，置百官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Murong De, following Yan's founding precedent, declared a first year, granted a general amnesty within his borders down from capital crimes, and established the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De then followed Later Yan's precedent, proclaimed his own inaugural reign, amnestied capital crimes and below, and set up a full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 以慕容麟為司空、領尚書令，慕容法為中軍將軍，慕輿拔為尚書左僕射，丁通為尚書右僕射，自余封授各有差。

translations.literal: Murong De appointed Murong Lin as minister of works and concurrent director of the secretariat, Murong Fa as general of the central army, Yu Ba as left vice-director of the secretariat, Ding Tong as right vice-director of the secretariat, and the rest received titles each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He named Murong Lin minister of works and chief of the secretariat, Murong Fa central-army general, Yu Ba senior vice-president of the secretariat, Ding Tong junior vice-president, and distributed other posts accordingly.

sentences.zh: 初，河間有麟見，慕容麟以為已瑞。

translations.literal: Earlier in Hejian a unicorn had appeared, and Murong Lin had taken it as an omen for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a qilin sighting in Hejian had led Murong Lin to claim it as his personal portent.

sentences.zh: 及此，潛謀為亂，事覺，賜死。

translations.literal: At this point Murong Lin secretly plotted rebellion; when the matter was discovered he was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: When his plot surfaced he was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 其夏，魏將賀賴盧率眾附之。

translations.literal: That summer Wei general Helai Lu led his masses to attach himself to Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Helai Lu of Wei brought his command over to Murong De's side.

sentences.zh: 至是，慕容寶自龍城南奔至黎陽，遣其中黃門令趙思召慕容鍾來迎。

translations.literal: At this point Murong Bao fled south from Longcheng to Liyang and sent his central yellow-gate director Zhao Si to summon Murong Zhong to come welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao then fled south from Longcheng to Liyang and dispatched Zhao Si, his central palace gate director, to call Murong Zhong to escort him.

sentences.zh: 鍾本首議勸德稱尊號，聞而惡之，執思付獄，馳使白狀。

translations.literal: Murong Zhong had originally been first to urge Murong De to assume the exalted title, and when he heard this he hated it, seized Zhao Si and handed him to prison, and galloped a messenger to report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhong, who had first urged Murong De to take the throne, took offense, jailed Zhao Si, and sent a courier to inform Murong De.

sentences.zh: 德謂其下曰：「卿等前以社稷大計，勸吾攝政。

translations.literal: Murong De told his subordinates that they had earlier, for the great plan of the altars of soil and grain, urged Murong De to take regency.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De told his followers they had pressed him into regency for the dynasty's sake.

sentences.zh: 吾亦以嗣帝奔亡，人神曠主，故權順群議，以系眾望。

translations.literal: Murong De also said that because the heir emperor was fleeing and men and spirits lacked a lord, he had temporarily yielded to the host's counsel in order to tie the multitude's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: He added that with the heir-apparent in flight and the realm leaderless, he had bowed to their advice to hold expectations together.

sentences.zh: 今天方悔禍，嗣帝得還，吾將具駕奉迎，謝罪行闕，然後角巾私第，卿等以為何如？

translations.literal: Now Heaven was beginning to repent the disaster, the heir emperor could return, and Murong De would prepare his carriage to greet him in welcome, apologize for his crimes at the palace gate, and afterward retire with a cornered headcloth to a private house, and he asked what they thought.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Heaven seemed to relent and the heir might return, he would ready his equipage to welcome Murong Bao, confess his faults at court, then withdraw to private life with a scholar's headwrap—what did they think?

sentences.zh: 」其黃門侍郎張華進曰：「夫爭奪之世，非雄才不振；

translations.literal: His gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Zhang Hua advanced and said that in an age of struggle only a heroic talent could rouse the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Zhang Hua replied that only a heroic figure could revive the state in an age of contention.

sentences.zh: 從橫之時，豈懦夫能濟！

translations.literal: In a time of maneuvering, how could a coward accomplish salvation?
translations.idiomatic: In a shifting balance of power no timid man could save the day.

sentences.zh: 陛下若蹈匹婦之仁，舍天授之業，威權一去，則身首不保，何退讓之有乎！

translations.literal: If His Majesty trod the kindness of a common wife, abandoned Heaven-bestowed enterprise, and authority and awesomeness departed, then body and head would not be preserved; what room was there for yielding?
translations.idiomatic: If Murong De indulged petty mercy, threw away a mandate Heaven had given him, and let power slip away, he would lose his life—there was no virtue in abdicating then.

sentences.zh: 」德曰：「吾以古人逆取順守，其道未足，所以中路徘徊，悵然未決耳。

translations.literal: Murong De said that he considered how the ancients seized in opposition and guarded in accord, and Murong De's way was not yet sufficient, so Murong De halted midway in hesitation and was despondent and undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De answered that the ancients took power boldly yet ruled legitimately, a balance he had not mastered, which left him torn and unresolved.

sentences.zh: 」慕輿護請馳問寶虛實，德流涕而遣之。

translations.literal: Yu Hu requested to gallop and inquire into Murong Bao's truth and falsehood, and Murong De wept as he sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hu volunteered to ride north and learn Murong Bao's true situation; Murong De sent him off in tears.

sentences.zh: 乃率壯士數百，隨思而北，因謀殺寶。

translations.literal: Yu Hu then led several hundred stalwarts and followed Zhao Si northward and plotted to kill Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: He led hundreds of picked men north with Zhao Si plotting to murder Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 初，寶遣思之後，知德攝位，懼而北奔。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Murong Bao had sent Zhao Si, he learned that Murong De had taken the position and was afraid and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: After dispatching Zhao Si, Murong Bao had learned of Murong De's assumption of power and fled north in fear.

sentences.zh: 護至無所見，執思而還。

translations.literal: When Yu Hu arrived he saw nothing, seized Zhao Si, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hu found no sign of Murong Bao, seized Zhao Si, and came back.

sentences.zh: 德以思閑習典故，將任之。

translations.literal: Murong De, because Zhao Si was versed in precedents and stories, was about to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De intended to employ Zhao Si for his knowledge of court precedent.

sentences.zh: 思曰：「昔關羽見重曹公，猶不忘先主之恩。

translations.literal: Zhao Si said that formerly Guan Yu was esteemed by Cao Cao yet did not forget his former lord's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Si replied that even Guan Yu, honored by Cao Cao, had not forgotten his first master's grace.

sentences.zh: 思雖刑餘賤隸，荷國寵靈，犬馬有心，而況人乎！

translations.literal: Though Zhao Si was a mutilated base slave who had received the state's favor, dogs and horses had hearts, how much more men.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was a castrated menial favored by the state, even dogs and horses kept loyalty—how much more a man.

sentences.zh: 乞還就上，以明微節。

translations.literal: Zhao Si begged to return to his superior in order to clarify his slight integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He begged leave to rejoin his sovereign and prove his humble loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」德固留之，思怒曰：「周室衰微，晉、鄭夾輔；

translations.literal: Murong De firmly detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De pressed him to stay.

sentences.zh: 漢有七國之難，實賴梁王。

translations.literal: Zhao Si grew angry and said that when the Zhou house declined, Jin and Zheng flanked it in support, and in Han there was the trouble of the seven states and in truth they relied on the Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Si angrily cited how Jin and Zheng buttressed declining Zhou and how the Prince of Liang had saved Han from the Rebellion of the Seven States.

sentences.zh: 殿下親則叔父，位則上臺，不能率先群後以匡王室，而幸根本之傾為趙倫之事。

translations.literal: His Highness in kinship was uncle yet in rank stood on the high terrace, yet could not lead the host of lords to aid the royal house, and instead rejoiced in the tipping of the root foundation to do the deeds of Zhao Lun.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's uncle and a minister of the highest rank, he should have rallied the lords to restore the house, yet he exploited the dynasty's peril like Sima Lun's usurpation.

sentences.zh: 思雖無申胥哭秦之效，猶慕君賓不生莽世。

translations.literal: Though Zhao Si lacked Shen Baoxu's effect of weeping at Qin, he still admired Junbin for not being born in Wang Mang's age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Si could not match Shen Baoxu's weeping at the court of Qin, yet he still envied Junbin for refusing to live under Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 」德怒，斬之。

translations.literal: De was angry and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De flew into a rage and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 晉南陽太守閭丘羨、甯朔將軍鄧啟方率眾二萬來伐，師次管城。

translations.literal: Jin Nanyang governor Lüqiu Xian and Ningshuo general Deng Qifang led twenty thousand men to attack; the army halted at Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin governor of Nanyang, Lüqiu Xian, and Ningshuo general Deng Qifang marched twenty thousand troops against him and encamped at Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 德遣其中軍慕容法、撫軍慕容和等距之，王師敗績。

translations.literal: De sent Central Army Murong Fa and Pacification General Murong He and others to resist them; the royal army suffered a rout.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De sent Central Army Murong Fa and Pacification General Murong He to meet them, and the Jin army was routed.

sentences.zh: 德怒法不窮追晉師，斬其撫軍司馬靳瑰。

translations.literal: De was angry that Fa did not pursue the Jin army to the limit, and beheaded his Pacification Army major Jin Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De blamed Murong Fa for breaking off the pursuit of the Jin force and executed his Pacification Army major Jin Gui.

sentences.zh: 初，苻登既為姚興所滅，登弟廣率部落降於德，拜冠軍將軍，處之乞活堡。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Fu Deng had been destroyed by Yao Xing, Deng's younger brother Fu Guang led his tribes to surrender to De; he was appointed Champion General and quartered at Qihuo Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Deng fell to Yao Xing, his brother Fu Guang led their followers to submit to Murong De, who named him Champion General and settled them at Qihuo Fort.

sentences.zh: 會熒惑守東井，或言秦當復興者，廣乃自稱秦王，敗德將慕容鐘。

translations.literal: When Mars occupied the Dongjing asterism, some said Qin would rise again; Guang then declared himself King of Qin and defeated De's general Murong Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Mars stood over Dongjing; some claimed Former Qin would revive. Fu Guang thereupon proclaimed himself King of Qin and routed Murong De's general Murong Zhong.

sentences.zh: 時德始都滑台，介於晉、魏之間，地無十城，眾不過數萬。

translations.literal: At that time De had just made Huatai his capital, caught between Jin and Wei, with fewer than ten cities and no more than a few tens of thousands of men.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De had only just set his capital at Huatai between Jin and Wei, holding fewer than ten towns and only a few tens of thousands of troops.

sentences.zh: 及鐘喪師，反側之徒多歸於廣。

translations.literal: When Zhong lost his army, wavering men mostly went over to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Zhong's defeat, many wavering followers went over to Fu Guang.

sentences.zh: 德乃留慕容和守滑台，親率眾討廣，斬之。

translations.literal: De then left Murong He to guard Huatai, personally led the host against Guang, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De left Murong He to hold Huatai, marched in person against Fu Guang, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 初，寶之至黎陽也，和長史李辯勸和納之，和不從。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Murong Bao reached Liyang, He's chief clerk Li Bian urged He to take Bao in, and He refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao came to Liyang, chief clerk Li Bian urged Murong He to admit him, but Murong He refused.

sentences.zh: 辯懼謀泄，乃引晉軍至管城，冀德親率師，於後作亂。

translations.literal: Bian feared the plot would leak, so drew Jin troops to Guancheng, hoping De would personally lead the army and he could raise trouble in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bian feared exposure, drew Jin troops to Guancheng, and hoped Murong De would take the field himself so Li Bian could raise revolt behind him.

sentences.zh: 會德不出，愈不自安。

translations.literal: But De did not go out, and Bian grew even more uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De did not march, and Li Bian grew still more anxious.

sentences.zh: 及德此行也，辯又勸和反，和不從。

translations.literal: On this expedition of De's, Bian again urged He to rebel, and He refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong De set out on this campaign, Li Bian again pressed Murong He to revolt, and Murong He again refused.

sentences.zh: 辯怒，殺和，以滑台降于魏。

translations.literal: Bian in anger killed He and surrendered Huatai to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bian slew Murong He in rage and handed Huatai over to Wei.

sentences.zh: 時將士家悉在城內，德將攻之，韓范言於德曰：「魏師已入城，據國成資，客主之勢，翻然復異，人情既危，不可以戰。

translations.literal: At that time officers' and soldiers' families were all inside the city; De was about to attack when Han Fan said to De, 'Wei troops have entered the city, hold the state and its resources; guest and host are reversed, hearts are shaken, and we cannot fight.'
translations.idiomatic: With every soldier's family inside the walls Murong De prepared to strike, but Han Fan said Wei held the town and its stores, the strategic balance had flipped, morale was brittle, and battle was unwise.

sentences.zh: 宜先據一方，為關中之基，然後畜力而圖之，計之上也。

translations.literal: 'We should first seize a region as a base for Guanzhong, then store strength and plan against them; that is the best plan.'
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan urged seizing a base like Guanzhong first, building strength, then striking back as the superior course.

sentences.zh: 」德乃止。

translations.literal: De then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De called off the assault.

sentences.zh: 德右衛將軍慕容雲斬李辯，率將士家累二萬餘人而出，三軍慶悅。

translations.literal: De's Right Guard general Murong Yun beheaded Li Bian, led more than twenty thousand officers' and soldiers' dependents out, and the three armies rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard general Murong Yun executed Li Bian and led out over twenty thousand dependents, to the army's delight.

sentences.zh: 德謀於眾曰：「苻廣雖平，而撫軍失據，進有強敵，退無所托，計將安出？

translations.literal: De consulted the host, saying, 'Though Fu Guang is crushed, the Pacification headquarters has lost its footing; advancing we face strong foes, retreating we have nowhere to lean; what plan should we take?'
translations.idiomatic: Murong De asked his court how to advance against strong enemies with no rear base now that Fu Guang was dead but Huatai was lost.

sentences.zh: 」張華進曰：「彭城阻帶山川，楚之舊都，地險人殷，可攻而據之，以為基本。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua stepped forward, saying, 'Pengcheng is girded by mountains and rivers, the old Chu capital; the ground is defensible and the people abundant; we can attack and hold it as our foundation.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua argued Pengcheng's terrain and wealth made it a capital worth taking by force.

sentences.zh: 」慕容鐘、慕輿護、封逞、韓𧨳等固勸攻滑台，潘聰曰：「滑台四通八達，非帝王之居。

translations.literal: Murong Zhong, Muyu Hu, Feng Cheng, Han Fan, and others strongly urged attacking Huatai; Pan Cong said, 'Huatai is a crossroads, not a place for an emperor to dwell.'
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhong, Muyu Hu, Feng Cheng, Han Fan, and others pressed to retake Huatai, while Pan Cong called it a hub ill suited to an imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 且北通大魏，西接強秦，此二國者，未可以高枕而待之。

translations.literal: 'Moreover it opens north to Great Wei and west joins strong Qin; these two states are not to be awaited lying easy on a pillow.'
translations.idiomatic: Pan Cong warned that Huatai lay open to Wei and to Yao Xing's Qin and could not be held with complacency.

sentences.zh: 彭城土曠人稀，地平無險，晉之歸鎮，必距王師。

translations.literal: 'Pengcheng has broad fields and thin population, flat ground without natural barriers; Jin's returning garrison is sure to block our royal army.'
translations.idiomatic: He added that Pengcheng was open ground where Jin would block Later Yan's advance.

sentences.zh: 又密邇江、淮，水路通浚，秋夏霖潦，千里為湖。

translations.literal: 'It also hugs the Yangzi and Huai; waterways reach Jun, and in autumn and summer rains turn a thousand li into lakes.'
translations.idiomatic: Pan Cong noted its nearness to the rivers, floods, and Jin's naval strength.

sentences.zh: 且水戰國之所短，吳之所長，今雖克之，非久安之計也。

translations.literal: 'Moreover water war is our state's short suit and Wu's long suit; even if we take it now, it is no plan for lasting peace.'
translations.idiomatic: He argued water fighting favored the southern foe, so even victory there would not secure Murong De long term.

sentences.zh: 青、齊沃壤，號曰東秦，土方二千，戶餘十萬，四塞之固，負海之饒，可謂用武之國。

translations.literal: 'Qing and Qi are fertile soil called Eastern Qin, two thousand li square, more than a hundred thousand households, boxed by four passes, rich with the sea; it may be called a land for wielding arms.'
translations.idiomatic: He praised Qi and Qing as Eastern Qin, populous, defensible, and rich for military power.

sentences.zh: 三齊英傑，蓄志以待，孰不思得明主以立尺寸之功！

translations.literal: 'The heroes of the three Qi have stored their will and wait; who does not long for a wise lord to win even slight merit!'
translations.idiomatic: Pan Cong said the Qi elite yearned for a worthy ruler to follow.

sentences.zh: 廣固者，曹嶷之所營，山川阻峻，足為帝王之都。

translations.literal: 'Guanggu was built by Cao Yi; its mountains and streams are steep enough for an emperor's capital.'
translations.idiomatic: He named Guanggu, Cao Yi's fortress, as defensible enough for a capital.

sentences.zh: 宜遣辯士馳說于前，大兵繼進於後，避閭渾昔負國恩，必翻然向化。

translations.literal: 'We should send eloquent men ahead to persuade, then follow with a great army; Bi Lü Hun once betrayed the state's grace and is sure to turn toward civilization.'
translations.idiomatic: He proposed envoys then an army, arguing Bi Lü Hun who had wronged Later Yan would flip or yield.

sentences.zh: 如其守迷不順，大軍臨之，自然瓦解。

translations.literal: 'If he clings to delusion and will not submit, when the great host reaches him he will naturally crumble.'
translations.idiomatic: If Bi Lü Hun resisted, Pan Cong expected him to collapse under pressure.

sentences.zh: 既據之後，閉關養銳，伺隙而動，此亦二漢之有關中、河內也。

translations.literal: 'Once we hold it, close the passes and nurse our edge, move when a gap opens; this too is like the two Han holding Guanzhong and Henei.'
translations.idiomatic: Holding Guanggu would mirror Han control of Guanzhong and Henei.

sentences.zh: 」德猶豫未決。

translations.literal: De still hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De remained undecided.

sentences.zh: 沙門郎公素知占候，德因訪其所適。

translations.literal: The monk Lang Gong was skilled in divination; De therefore asked him where they should go.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De consulted the monk Lang Gong, versed in astrology.

sentences.zh: 郎曰：「敬覽三策，潘尚書之議可謂興邦之術矣。

translations.literal: Lang said, 'I have reviewed the three plans; Minister Pan's counsel may be called a method to raise the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Lang Gong endorsed Pan Cong's strategy as state building.

sentences.zh: 今歲初，長星起于奎婁，遂掃虛危，而虛危，齊之分野，除舊佈新之象。

translations.literal: 'At the year's start a long comet rose in Kui and Lou, then swept Xu and Wei; Xu and Wei are Qi's field division, an omen of removing the old and spreading the new.'
translations.idiomatic: He read a comet over Xu and Wei as Qi's astrological field and an omen of renewal.

sentences.zh: 宜先定舊魯，巡撫琅邪，待秋風戒節，然後北圍臨齊，天之道也。

translations.literal: 'We should first secure old Lu, pacify Langye on tour, wait until the autumn wind sets the season, then invest Linqi from the north; that is Heaven's way.'
translations.idiomatic: He urged securing Lu, touring Langye, then besieging Linqi in autumn as Heaven's course.

sentences.zh: 」德大悅，引師而南，兗州北鄙諸縣悉降，置守宰以撫之。

translations.literal: De was greatly pleased, led the army south, and all counties on the northern border of Yanzhou submitted; he set governors to soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De marched south, winning the north of Yanzhou and installing officials.

sentences.zh: 存問高年，軍無私掠，百姓安之，牛酒屬路。

translations.literal: He inquired after the aged, the army took no private plunder, the common people were at peace, and oxen and wine lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: His troops refrained from looting, elders were cared for, and locals brought food and drink to the road.

sentences.zh: 德遣使喻齊郡太守避閭渾，渾不從，遣慕容鐘率步騎二萬擊之。

translations.literal: De sent envoys to instruct Qi commandery governor Bi Lü Hun; Hun refused, so De sent Murong Zhong with twenty thousand foot and horse to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De summoned Bi Lü Hun in Qi commandery; when he refused, Murong Zhong attacked with twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 德進據琅邪，徐、兗之土附者十餘萬，自琅邪而北，迎者四萬餘人。

translations.literal: De advanced and occupied Langye; more than a hundred thousand men of Xu and Yanzhou attached, and north from Langye over forty thousand came to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Taking Langye, Murong De drew over a hundred thousand from Xu and Yanzhou and forty thousand more north of Langye.

sentences.zh: 德進寇莒城，守將任安委城而遁，以潘聰鎮莒城。

translations.literal: De advanced against Ju city; defending general Ren An abandoned the city and fled, and De set Pan Cong to hold Ju.
translations.idiomatic: He took Ju as garrison commander Ren An fled, leaving Pan Cong to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 鐘傳檄青州諸郡曰：「隆替有時，義列昔經；

translations.literal: Zhong circulated a call to Qingzhou's commanderies, saying, 'Rise and fall have their seasons, righteousness is arrayed in the classics of old.'
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhong's proclamation to Qingzhou cited fate and classical precedent.

sentences.zh: 困難啟聖，事彰中籙。

translations.literal: 'Hardship opens the way for a sage; the matter shines in the middle talisman.'
translations.idiomatic: He claimed crisis revealed the destined sage ruler.

sentences.zh: 是以宣王龍飛于危周，光武鳳起於絕漢，斯蓋歷數大期，帝王之興廢也。

translations.literal: 'Therefore King Xuan of Zhou soared from perilous Zhou, Guangwu of Han rose from dying Han; these are the great cycles by which emperors rise and fall.'
translations.idiomatic: He compared Later Yan to King Xuan and Emperor Guangwu reviving ruined dynasties.

sentences.zh: 自我永康多難，長鯨逸網，華夏四分，黎元五裂。

translations.literal: 'From our Yongkang troubles onward, the great whale slipped the net, Huaxia split four ways, and the people were torn five ways.'
translations.idiomatic: He described the realm's fragmentation after Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 逆賊辟閭渾父蔚，昔同段龕阻亂淄川，太宰東征，剿絕凶命。

translations.literal: 'The rebel Bi Lü Hun's father Wei once joined Duan Kan blocking chaos on the Zi River; the grand preceptor marched east and extirpated the wicked life.'
translations.idiomatic: He accused Bi Lü Hun's father Bi Wei of banditry with Duan Kan until Later Yan's eastern campaign extirpated them.

sentences.zh: 渾于覆巢之下，蒙全卵之施，曾微犬馬識養之心，復襲凶父樂禍之志，盜據東秦，遠附吳、越，割剝黎元，委輸南海。

translations.literal: 'Under an overturned nest Hun received the favor of a spared egg, yet showed not the heart of a dog or horse toward nurture, again taking his wicked father's joy in disaster, stealing Eastern Qin, attaching far to Wu and Yue, flaying the people and shipping tribute to the southern sea.'
translations.idiomatic: He said Bi Lü Hun survived Later Yan's mercy yet oppressed Qi, courted the south, and exploited the people.

sentences.zh: 皇上應期，大命再集，矜彼營丘，暫阻王略，故以七州之眾二十餘萬，巡省貸宗，問罪齊、魯。

translations.literal: 'Our sovereign answers the season; the great mandate gathers again; pitying Yingqiu he briefly blocks the royal plan, hence with the hosts of seven provinces over two hundred thousand he tours to aid the clan and calls Qi and Lu to account.'
translations.idiomatic: He framed Murong De's great army as punishing Qi and Lu for sheltering Bi Lü Hun at Yingqiu.

sentences.zh: 昔韓信以裨將伐齊，有征無戰；

translations.literal: 'Formerly Han Xin as a subordinate general attacked Qi with a campaign and no battle.'
translations.idiomatic: He likened the campaign to Han Xin's swift conquest of Qi.

sentences.zh: 耿弇以偏軍討步，克不移朔。

translations.literal: 'Geng Yan with a detached force attacked Bu and conquered without shifting the month.'
translations.idiomatic: He cited Geng Yan's rapid victory over Bu Mao.

sentences.zh: 況以萬乘之師，掃一隅之寇，傾山碎卵，方之非易。

translations.literal: 'How much more with hosts of ten thousand chariots sweeping a corner bandit, toppling mountains and smashing eggs; compared to that it is not hard.'
translations.idiomatic: A Later Yan host could crush a corner rebel more easily still.

sentences.zh: 孤以不才，忝荷先驅，都督元戎一十二萬，皆烏丸突騎，三河猛士，奮劍與夕火爭光，揮戈與秋月競色。

translations.literal: 'I, lacking talent, shamefully bear the vanguard, commanding one hundred twenty thousand of the main army, all Wuhuan shock cavalry and fierce men of the three He, swords vying with evening fires, spears rivaling autumn moons.'
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhong boasted one hundred twenty thousand picked cavalry and infantry under his command.

sentences.zh: 以此攻城，何城不克；

translations.literal: 'With this to storm a city, what city would not fall?'
translations.idiomatic: No city could withstand such an assault.

sentences.zh: 以此眾戰，何敵不平！

translations.literal: 'With this host to fight, what foe would not be pacified!'
translations.idiomatic: No enemy could stand against that force.

sentences.zh: 昔竇融以河西歸漢，榮被于後裔；

translations.literal: 'Formerly Dou Rong brought Hexi to Han and glory spread to his descendants.'
translations.idiomatic: Dou Rong's submission to Han brought lasting honor.

sentences.zh: 彭寵盜逆漁陽，身死于奴僕。

translations.literal: 'Peng Chong rebelled at Yuyang and died at the hands of slaves.'
translations.idiomatic: Peng Chong's revolt ended in ignominious death.

sentences.zh: 近則曹嶷跋扈，見擒于後趙；

translations.literal: 'Recently Cao Yi ran riot and was captured by Later Zhao.'
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi's arrogance ended in capture by Later Zhao.

sentences.zh: 段龕幹紀，取滅於前朝。

translations.literal: 'Duan Kan violated the norm and was extinguished by the prior court.'
translations.idiomatic: Duan Kan's breach of order brought destruction under the previous regime.

sentences.zh: 此非古今之吉凶，已然之成敗乎？

translations.literal: 'Are these not the good and ill of ancient and modern, the success and failure already settled?'
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhong asked whether history did not show clear outcomes.

sentences.zh: 渾若先迷後悟，榮寵有加。

translations.literal: 'If Hun first errs then awakens, honor and favor will increase.'
translations.idiomatic: Bi Lü Hun would be richly rewarded if he repented.

sentences.zh: 如其敢抗王師，敗滅必無遺燼。

translations.literal: 'If he dares resist the royal army, defeat and extinction will leave not even embers.'
translations.idiomatic: Resistance would mean total annihilation.

sentences.zh: 稷下之雄，岱北之士，有能斬送渾者，賞同佐命。

translations.literal: 'Heroes of Jixia and knights north of Dai who can behead Hun and deliver him shall share the reward of founding ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: He offered founding minister rank for Bi Lü Hun's head.

sentences.zh: 脫履機不發，必玉石俱摧。

translations.literal: 'If the moment is missed, jade and stone alike will be shattered.'
translations.idiomatic: If men missed the chance to defect, victor and vanquished alike would be ruined.

sentences.zh: 」渾聞德軍將至，從八千餘家入廣固。

translations.literal: Hearing De's army was coming, Hun led more than eight thousand households into Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Murong De's approach, Bi Lü Hun moved over eight thousand households into Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 諸郡皆承檄降於德。

translations.literal: All commanderies accepted the summons and surrendered to De.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies submitted to Murong De on Murong Zhong's summons.

sentences.zh: 渾懼，將妻子奔于魏。

translations.literal: Hun was afraid and, taking wife and children, fled toward Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Lü Hun fled toward Wei with his family.

sentences.zh: 德遣射聲校尉劉綱追斬於莒城。

translations.literal: De sent She Sheng colonel Liu Gang to pursue and behead him at Ju city.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De sent She Sheng colonel Liu Gang to run him down and execute him at Ju.

sentences.zh: 渾參軍張瑛常與渾作檄，辭多不遜。

translations.literal: Hun's aide Zhang Ying had often drafted proclamations with Hun, and the language was mostly insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Lü Hun's staff officer Zhang Ying had co-written strident edicts with him.

sentences.zh: 及此，德擒而讓之。

translations.literal: At this point De seized him and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De captured Zhang Ying and reproached him.

sentences.zh: 瑛神色自若，徐對曰：「渾之有臣，猶韓信之有蒯通。

translations.literal: Ying was calm in mien and slowly replied, 'Hun having a subject is like Han Xin having Kuai Tong.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying calmly compared himself to Kuai Tong serving Han Xin under Bi Lü Hun.

sentences.zh: 通遇漢祖而蒙恕，臣遭陛下而嬰戮，比之古人，竊為不幸。

translations.literal: 'Kuai met the Han founder and was spared; your subject meets Your Majesty and suffers execution; compared to the ancients, I privately count it misfortune.'
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Tong was spared while he faced death, which he called ill luck beside the precedent.

sentences.zh: 防風之誅，臣實甘之，但恐堯、舜之化未弘于四海耳。

translations.literal: 'The execution of Fangfeng I would truly accept; I only fear Yao and Shun's transforming influence has not spread across the four seas.'
translations.idiomatic: He accepted guilt like Fangfeng yet hinted Murong De lacked sage kings' virtue.

sentences.zh: 」德初善其言，後竟殺之。

translations.literal: De at first praised his words but in the end still killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De first admired the answer but still executed Zhang Ying.

sentences.zh: 德遂入廣固。

translations.literal: De then entered Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De marched into Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 四年，僭即皇帝位於南郊，大赦，改元為建平，設行廟于宮南，遣使奉策告成焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he usurped the emperor's title at the southern suburb, issued a general amnesty, changed the era name to Jianping, set a traveling temple south of the palace, and sent envoys with the document to report completion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he took the imperial title at the southern altar, amnestied the realm, adopted the Jianping era, placed a mobile temple south of the palace, and dispatched envoys to announce the deed.

sentences.zh: 進慕容鐘為司徒，慕輿拔為司空，封孚為左僕射，慕輿護為右僕射。

translations.literal: He advanced Murong Zhong to Minister of Education, Muyu Ba to Minister of Works, Feng Fu to Left Director, and Muyu Hu to Right Director of the Department of State.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Murong Zhong to steward, Muyu Ba to minister of works, Feng Fu and Muyu Hu as left and right directors.

sentences.zh: 遣其度支尚書封愷、中書侍郎封逞觀省風俗，所在大饗將士。

translations.literal: He sent his revenue minister Feng Kai and palace aide Feng Cheng to inspect customs, feasting officers everywhere they went.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Feng Kai and Feng Cheng to tour local customs and feast the troops.

sentences.zh: 以其妻段氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He made his wife Lady Duan empress.
translations.idiomatic: He named his consort Lady Duan empress.

sentences.zh: 建立學官，簡公卿已下子弟及二品士門二百人為太學生。

translations.literal: He established schools, selecting two hundred sons of dukes and ministers down to second rank gentry households as academy students.
translations.idiomatic: He founded an academy with two hundred students from elite families.

sentences.zh: 後因宴其群臣，酒酣，笑而言曰：「朕雖寡薄，恭己南面而朝諸侯，在上不驕，夕惕於位，可方自古何等主也？

translations.literal: Later at a banquet for his ministers, when the wine was warm he laughed and said, 'Though I am meager, I reverently face south to court the lords; not proud on high, anxious at my post by night; with whom among the ancients may I be compared?'
translations.idiomatic: Drunk at court he asked which classical ruler his modest diligent reign resembled.

sentences.zh: 」其青州刺史鞠仲曰：「陛下中興之聖後，少康、光武之儔也。

translations.literal: His Qingzhou governor Ju Zhong said, 'Your Majesty is a sagely restorer of the middle revival, the peer of Shaokang and Guangwu.'
translations.idiomatic: Ju Zhong compared him to Shaokang and Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 」德顧命左右賜仲帛千匹。

translations.literal: De ordered attendants to grant Zhong a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De told his staff to award Ju Zhong a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 仲以賜多為讓，德曰：「卿知調朕，朕不知調卿乎！

translations.literal: Zhong demurred because the gift was large; De said, 'You know how to tease me; do I not know how to tease you?'
translations.idiomatic: When Ju Zhong objected to the lavish gift Murong De called it banter for banter.

sentences.zh: 卿飾對非實，故亦以虛言相賞，賞不謬加，何足謝也！

translations.literal: 'You adorned your answer with what was not true, so I also reward you with empty words; the reward is not wrongly piled; what is there to thank for?'
translations.idiomatic: Murong De said Ju Zhong's flattery earned a joking reward that need not be refused.

sentences.zh: 」韓範進曰：「臣聞天子無戲言，忠臣無妄對。

translations.literal: Han Fan stepped forward, saying, 'I have heard the Son of Heaven has no jesting words and loyal ministers have no reckless answers.'
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan objected that rulers should not jest and ministers should not dissemble.

sentences.zh: 今日之論，上下相欺，可謂君臣俱失。

translations.literal: 'Today's discussion has ruler and subject deceiving each other; it may be called both sides failing.'
translations.idiomatic: He called the exchange mutual deception and a failure for both sides.

sentences.zh: 」德大悅，賜範絹五十匹。

translations.literal: De was greatly pleased and granted Fan fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De delighted in the rebuke and gave Han Fan fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 自是昌言競進，朝多直士矣。

translations.literal: From then forth straight speech vied to advance and the court had many honest men.
translations.idiomatic: Frank counsel flourished and the court gained upright officials.

sentences.zh: 德母兄先在長安，遣平原人杜弘如長安問存否，弘曰：「臣至長安，若不奉太后動止，便即西如張掖，以死為效。

translations.literal: De's mother and elder brother were first in Chang'an; he sent Pingyuan man Du Hong to Chang'an to ask whether they still lived, and Hong said, 'If I reach Chang'an and do not bring back news of the empress dowager's condition, I will go west to Zhangye and die to prove my loyalty.'
translations.idiomatic: Murong De sent Du Hong to Chang'an for news of his mother and brother, and Du Hong vowed to reach Zhangye or die trying if he failed.

sentences.zh: 臣父雄年逾六十，未沾榮貴，乞本縣之祿，以申烏鳥之情。

translations.literal: 'My father Xiong is past sixty and has not tasted honor; I beg the salary of our home county to express the crow's filial heart.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong asked a county stipend for his aging father to show filial duty.

sentences.zh: 」張華進曰：「杜弘未行而求祿，要利情深，不可使也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua stepped forward, saying, 'Du Hong has not yet gone but seeks salary; his desire for profit runs deep; he cannot be used.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua called Du Hong venal for asking pay before departing.

sentences.zh: 」德曰：「吾方散所輕之財，招所重之死，況為親尊而可吝乎！

translations.literal: De said, 'I am now scattering the wealth I lightly esteem to recruit the deaths I heavily value; how could I be stingy for a revered kinsman?'
translations.idiomatic: Murong De refused to withhold reward for a mission to fetch his kin.

sentences.zh: 且弘為君迎親，為父求祿，雖外如要利，內實忠孝。

translations.literal: 'Moreover Hong goes for the ruler to welcome kin and for his father seeks salary; though outwardly like seeking profit, inwardly it is loyalty and filial piety.'
translations.idiomatic: He read Du Hong's request as loyalty and filial piety beneath a mercenary surface.

sentences.zh: 」乃以雄為平原令。

translations.literal: He therefore appointed Xiong governor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De named Du Xiong magistrate of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 弘至張掖，為盜所殺，德聞而悲之，厚撫其妻子。

translations.literal: Hong reached Zhangye and was killed by bandits; De heard and grieved, treating his wife and children generously.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong was killed by bandits at Zhangye; Murong De mourned him and richly aided his family.

sentences.zh: 明年，德如齊城，登營丘，望晏嬰塚，顧謂左右曰：「禮，大夫不逼城葬。

translations.literal: The next year De went to Qi city, climbed Yingqiu, gazed on Yan Ying's mound, and said to those around him, 'By ritual a great officer is not buried pressing the city wall.'
translations.idiomatic: The next year atop Yingqiu Murong De wondered at Yan Ying's tomb near the walls against ritual.

sentences.zh: 平仲古之賢人，達禮者也，而生居近市，死葬近城，豈有意乎？

translations.literal: 'Pingzhong was a worthy of old, one who understood ritual, yet lived near the market in life and is buried near the city in death; did he intend it?'
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether the sage Yan Ying meant to lie so close to the market and walls.

sentences.zh: 」青州秀才晏謨對曰：「孔子稱臣先人平仲賢，則賢矣。

translations.literal: Qingzhou xiucai Yan Mo replied, 'Confucius called my ancestor Pingzhong worthy; worthy he was.'
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou graduate Yan Mo noted Confucius had praised his forebear Yan Ying.

sentences.zh: 豈不知高其梁，豐其禮？

translations.literal: 'Could he not have known to raise his ridgepole and enrich his rites?'
translations.idiomatic: Yan Mo implied Yan Ying chose humility over pomp despite knowing better.

sentences.zh: 蓋政在家門，故儉以矯世。

translations.literal: In sum government was in the family gate, therefore he used frugality to correct the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Mo explained that Yan Ying kept government in the family and used austerity to set the tone for his age.

sentences.zh: 存居湫隘，卒豈擇地而葬乎！

translations.literal: He lived in a cramped low place; at death could he choose ground to bury!
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a mean alley—at death could he pick his burial ground?

sentences.zh: 所以不遠門者，猶冀悟平生意也。

translations.literal: The reason he did not distance the gate was still hoping to awaken Pingzhong's intent in life.
translations.idiomatic: He lay close to the gate because he still hoped to echo Yan Ying's lifelong intent.

sentences.zh: 」遂以謨從至漢城陽景王廟，宴庶老于申池，北登社首山，東望鼎足，因目牛山而歎曰：「古無不死！

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Yan Mo along to the temple of Prince Jing of Chengyang at Hancheng, feasted the common elders at Shen Pool, climbed north Mount Sheshou, looked east at the tripod legs of terrain, then gazed at Mount Niu and sighed, saying, 'From antiquity there has been no not dying!'
translations.idiomatic: He brought Yan Mo to the Han-era temple of Prince Jing of Chengyang, feasted elders at Shen Pool, climbed Sheshou, looked toward the tripod hills, then gazed at Mount Niu and sighed that no one escapes death.

sentences.zh: 」愴然有終焉之志。

translations.literal: He was mournful and had the will to end there.
translations.idiomatic: He was overcome with melancholy and half wished to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 遂問謨以齊之山川丘陵，賢哲舊事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he asked Yan Mo about Qi mountains and rivers, mounds and hills, worthies and ancient affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He quizzed Yan Mo on Qi's geography and famous stories.

sentences.zh: 謨曆對詳辯，畫地成圖。

translations.literal: Yan Mo answered in sequence, detailed and disputatious, and drew lines on the ground to make a map.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Mo answered in fluent detail and sketched a map in the dust.

sentences.zh: 德深嘉之，拜尚書郎。

translations.literal: De deeply praised him and appointed him gentleman of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De was so impressed he named him a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 立冶于商山，置鹽官于烏常澤，以廣軍國之用。

translations.literal: He set up smelting works on Mount Shang and salt offices at Wuchang Marsh to broaden military and state use.
translations.idiomatic: He opened ironworks on Mount Shang and salt monopolies at Wuchang Marsh to swell the army's coffers.

sentences.zh: 德故吏趙融自長安來，始具母兄凶問，德號慟吐血，因而寢疾。

translations.literal: De's former clerk Zhao Rong came from Chang'an and first brought full news of the mourning for mother and elder brother; De wailed and spat blood, and on that account took to bed ill.
translations.idiomatic: His old clerk Zhao Rong arrived from Chang'an with word of his mother and brother's deaths; Murong De howled until he coughed blood and fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 其司隸校尉慕容達因此謀反，遣牙門皇璆率眾攻端門，殿中師侯赤眉開門應之。

translations.literal: His metropolitan commandant Murong Da thereupon plotted rebellion, sent gate guard Huang Kui to lead a host attacking the Duan Gate, and palace instructor Hou Chimei opened the gate in response.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan commandant Murong Da seized the moment to rebel, sent Huang Kui against the Duan Gate, and won inside help from Hou Chimei.

sentences.zh: 中黃門遜進扶德逾城，隱於進舍。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Xun Jin helped De over the wall and hid him in a forward lodging.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch helped Murong De over the wall into hiding.

sentences.zh: 段宏等聞宮中有變，勒兵屯四門。

translations.literal: Duan Hong and others heard there was turmoil in the palace and led troops to camp at the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hong and the rest heard the alarm and sealed the four gates with troops.

sentences.zh: 德入宮，誅赤眉等，達懼而奔魏。

translations.literal: De entered the palace, executed Chimei and the rest, and Da fled in fear to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De re-entered the palace, executed Hou Chimei's faction, and Murong Da fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 慕容法及魏師戰於濟北之摽榆俗，魏師敗績。

translations.literal: Murong Fa together with Wei troops fought north of Ji at Biaoyu ford; Wei troops suffered a rout.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Fa clashed with Wei north of Ji near Biaoyu and routed them.

sentences.zh: 其尚書韓𧨳上疏曰：「二寇逋誅，國恥未雪，關西為豺鋃之藪，楊越為鴟鴞之林，三京社稷，鞠為丘墟，四祖園陵，蕪而不守，豈非義夫憤歎之日，烈士忘身之秋。

translations.literal: His minister Han Fan submitted a memorial saying, 'The two bandits roam unpunished, national shame is not washed away; west of the pass is a den of wolves, Yang and Yue are a forest of owls; the three capitals' altars have become mounds, the four ancestors' mausoleums lie weed-choked and undefended—is this not the day for righteous men to sigh and for knights to forget their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan memorialized that Western Qin and Eastern Jin still shamed the dynasty, the old capitals lay in ruins, and loyal men should ache to strike.

sentences.zh: 而皇室多難，威略未振，是使長蛇弗翦，封豕假息。

translations.literal: Yet the royal house has many hardships and martial awe has not yet risen, so the long serpent is not cut and the great boar catches its breath.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the house of Jin still staggered, so great evils went unstruck.

sentences.zh: 人懷憤慨，常謂一日之安不可以永久，終朝之逸無卒歲之憂。

translations.literal: Men harbor indignation, always saying a single day's peace cannot last forever, a morning's ease brings no year's rest.
translations.idiomatic: People muttered that a morning's peace bought no lasting safety.

sentences.zh: 陛下中興大業，務在遵養，矜遷萌之失土，假長復而不役，湣黎庶之息肩，貴因循而不擾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's restoration enterprise stresses compliance and nurturing, pitying displaced refugees' lost lands and granting long recovery without corvée, sympathizing with the people's rested shoulders and prizing continuity without harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De's policy favored mercy, light taxes, and rest for the people.

sentences.zh: 斯可以保甯于營丘，難以經措于秦、越。

translations.literal: This can preserve peace at Yingqiu but is hard to apply to Qin and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: That could secure Shandong but would not recover the deep south or the northwest.

sentences.zh: 今群凶僭逆，實繁有徒，據我三方，伺國瑕釁。

translations.literal: Now many villains usurp and rebel, truly a host of followers hold our three sides and watch for cracks in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels still held three fronts against him.

sentences.zh: 深宜審量虛實，大校成敗，養兵厲甲，廣農積糧，進為雪恥討寇之資，退為山河萬全之固。

translations.literal: It is deeply fitting to weigh void and substance, broadly gauge victory and defeat, nurture troops and harden armor, widen farming and pile grain, advance as capital to wash shame and punish bandits, retreat as a ten-thousand-li bulwark of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan urged building food and forces for offense and defense.

sentences.zh: 而百姓因秦、晉之弊，迭相陰憲，或百室合戶，或千丁共籍，依託城社，不懼燻燒，公避課役，擅為奸宄，損風毀憲，法所不容，但檢今未宣，弗可加戮。

translations.literal: Yet the common people, inheriting the harm of Qin and Jin, successively conspire in shadow; some hundred households share one register, some thousand adult males share one roll, relying on altars of soil and grain and fearing no burning, publicly avoiding taxes and labor, recklessly acting treacherous, harming custom and destroying statutes—what the law cannot tolerate—but because inspection has not yet been proclaimed, we cannot yet add execution.
translations.idiomatic: He described tax evasion through hidden households and urged registration reform before harsher punishments.

sentences.zh: 今宜隱實黎萌，正其編貫，庶上增皇朝理物之明，下益軍國兵資之用。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to reveal the truth about the common folk, correct their household rolls, so above we increase the court's clarity in ordering things, below we add to army and state use of soldiers and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Registering real households would help revenue and justice.

sentences.zh: 若蒙採納，冀裨山海，雖遇商鞅之刑，悅綰之害，所不辭也。

translations.literal: If this be adopted, I hope to add to mountain and sea; though I meet Shang Yang's punishments or Yue Wan's harm, I would not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan offered to carry the policy even at personal risk.

sentences.zh: 」德納之，遣其車騎將軍慕容鎮率騎三千，緣邊嚴防，備百姓逃竄。

translations.literal: De accepted it and sent chariot-and-cavalry general Murong Zhen with three thousand horse to patrol the border strictly and guard against commoners fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De agreed and sent Murong Zhen to seal the frontier against flight.

sentences.zh: 以𧨳為使持節、散騎常侍、行台尚書，巡郡縣隱實，得廕戶五萬八千。

translations.literal: He appointed Han Fan as commissioner bearing credentials, regular attendant for scattered cavalry, acting director of the traveling headquarters, to tour commanderies and counties and reveal truth, obtaining fifty-eight thousand hidden households.
translations.idiomatic: He named Han Fan inspector and uncovered fifty-eight thousand concealed households.

sentences.zh: 𧨳公廉正直，所在野次，人不擾焉。

translations.literal: Han Fan was fair, incorrupt, and upright; wherever he went he camped in the open and people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan camped in the fields and never troubled the locals.

sentences.zh: 德大集諸生，親臨策試。

translations.literal: De greatly gathered the students and personally attended the policy examination.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De convened the academy and presided over the examinations himself.

sentences.zh: 既而饗宴，乘高遠矚，顧謂其尚書魯邃曰：「齊、魯固多君子，當昔全盛之時，接、慎、巴生、淳于、鄒、田之徒，廕修簷，臨清沼，馳硃輪，佩長劍，恣非馬之雄辭，奮談天之逸辯，指麾則紅紫成章，俯仰則丘陵生韻，至於今日，荒草頹墳，氣消煙滅，永言千載，能不依然！

translations.literal: Presently he feasted, rode high and looked far, and said to his minister Lu Sui, 'Qi and Lu surely had many gentlemen; in their full splendor men like Jie, Shen, Ba Sheng, Chunyu, Zou, and Tian sheltered under broad eaves, leaned on clear pools, raced vermillion wheels, wore long swords, vented heroic rhetoric, raised heaven-storming debate, gestured and purple and red formed patterns, bowed and hills and mounds took rhythm; down to today wild grass and ruined tombs, breath gone smoke extinguished—speaking of a thousand years, how can one not be moved!'
translations.idiomatic: Over wine he mourned to Lu Sui how Qi's literati had vanished into weed-covered graves.

sentences.zh: 」邃答曰：「武王封比干之墓，漢祖祭信陵之墳，皆留心賢哲，每懷往事。

translations.literal: Sui replied, 'King Wu of Zhou closed Bi Gan's tomb, Han's Gaozu sacrificed at Lord Xinling's grave—both fixed their hearts on worthies and often cherished old deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sui compared him to rulers who honored ancient worthies' graves.

sentences.zh: 陛下慈深二主，澤被九泉，若使彼而有知，寧不銜荷矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's kindness runs deeper than those two lords, your grace reaches the nine springs; if they had consciousness, how would they not bear gratitude in their mouths!'
translations.idiomatic: He said Murong De's kindness outshamed King Wu and Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 先是，妖賊王始聚眾於太山，自稱太平皇帝，號其父為太上皇，兄為征東將軍，弟征西將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, demon bandit Wang Shi gathered a host at Mount Tai, styled himself emperor of Great Peace, titled his father retired emperor, elder brother general who campaigns east, younger brother general who campaigns west.
translations.idiomatic: A charlatan named Wang Shi had declared himself emperor on Mount Tai with a full family of bogus titles.

sentences.zh: 慕容鎮討擒之，斬於都市。

translations.literal: Murong Zhen campaigned, captured him, and beheaded him in the great market.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhen took him and executed him publicly.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，或問其父及兄弟所在，始答曰：「太上皇帝蒙塵於外，征東、征西亂兵所害。

translations.literal: At execution someone asked where his father and brothers were; Shi answered, 'The retired emperor wanders in dust without, the east and west generals were killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the block he claimed his imperial kin were 'in exile' or dead to mutiny.

sentences.zh: 惟朕一身，獨無聊賴。

translations.literal: 'Only I alone remain, utterly without support.'
translations.idiomatic: Only I, he said, was left alive.

sentences.zh: 」其妻怒之曰：「止坐此口，以至於此，奈何復爾！

translations.literal: His wife angrily said, 'It is only because of this mouth that you reached this; how can you do it again!'
translations.idiomatic: His wife snapped that his big mouth had doomed him.

sentences.zh: 」始曰：「皇后！

translations.literal: Shi said, 'Empress!'
translations.idiomatic: He answered, 'My empress!'

sentences.zh: 自古豈有不破之家，不亡之國邪！

translations.literal: 'From antiquity has there been a house that never broke, a state that never perished!'
translations.idiomatic: He asked if any dynasty lasted forever.

sentences.zh: 」行刑者以刀環築之，仰視曰：「崩即崩矣，終不改帝號。

translations.literal: The executioner struck him with the ring of the blade; looking up he said, 'Collapse it may collapse, I will never change the imperial title.'
translations.idiomatic: Even as the headsman's blade rang on his skull he insisted on his emperor title.

sentences.zh: 」德聞而哂之。

translations.literal: De heard and sneered.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De only laughed.

sentences.zh: 時桓玄將行篡逆，誅不附己者。

translations.literal: At that time Huan Xuan's general was about to usurp and killed those who would not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan prepared his coup he purged dissenters.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史劉軌、襄城太守司馬休之、征虜將軍劉敬宣、廣陵相高雅之、江都長張誕並內不自安，皆奔於德。

translations.literal: Ji Province inspector Liu Gui, Xiangcheng prefect Sima Xiuzhi, general who captures barbarians Liu Jingxuan, Guangling chancellor Gao Yazhi, and Jiangdu magistrate Zhang Dan all felt insecure within and fled to De.
translations.idiomatic: Several Jin officials fled north to Murong De.

sentences.zh: 於是德中書侍郎韓范上疏曰：「夫帝王之道，必崇經略。

translations.literal: Thereupon De's palace aide Han Fan submitted a memorial saying, 'The way of emperors and kings must honor planning and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan urged exploiting Huan Xuan's usurpation.

sentences.zh: 有其時無其人，則弘濟之功闕；

translations.literal: Having the time without the man, then the work of great rescue is lacking;
translations.idiomatic: When the hour strikes but no worthy leader stands forward, no great restoration can be achieved.

sentences.zh: 有其人無其時，則英武之志不申。

translations.literal: Having the man without the time, then heroic martial intent is not displayed.
translations.idiomatic: When a capable man lacks the right season, even heroic designs cannot take flight.

sentences.zh: 至於能成王業者，惟人時合也。

translations.literal: As for those able to complete kingly work, only when man and time align.
translations.idiomatic: True success needed man and heaven in accord.

sentences.zh: 自晉國內難，七載於茲。

translations.literal: Since Jin's internal disaster, seven years have passed here.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years had passed since Jin's internal collapse.

sentences.zh: 桓玄逆篡，虐逾董卓，神怒人怨，其殃積矣。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan usurped in rebellion, his cruelty surpassing Dong Zhuo; gods angry and men resentful, his calamities are piled.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan called Huan Xuan worse than Dong Zhuo and ripe for attack.

sentences.zh: 可乘之機，莫過此也。

translations.literal: A chance to strike exceeds none other than this.
translations.idiomatic: No opportunity could top the present.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之神武，經而緯之，驅樂奮之卒，接厭亂之機，譬猶聲發回應，形動影隨，未足比其易也。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's divine martial quality, ordering warp and weft, driving troops eager for joy, joining a world weary of chaos, it is like sound issuing and echo answering, form moving and shadow following—not enough to compare its ease.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De could crush him as easily as echo follows sound.

sentences.zh: 且江、淮南北戶口未幾，公私戎馬不過數百，守備之事蓋亦微矣。
