translations.literal: Moreover north and south of the Yangzi and Huai households are still few; public and private war horses number only in the hundreds; matters of defense are also slight.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's lower Yangzi defenses were still thin.

sentences.zh: 若以步騎一萬，建雷霆之舉，卷甲長驅，指臨江、會，必望旗草偃，壺漿屬路。

translations.literal: If with ten thousand foot and horse we raise a thunderstroke, roll armor in a long drive, point to Linjiang and Kuaiji, they are sure to lower banners like grass bending, and jars of broth will line the road.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand men could sweep to the lower Yangzi and meet surrender.

sentences.zh: 跨地數千，眾逾十萬，可以西並強秦，北抗大魏。

translations.literal: Spanning several thousand li, hosts exceeding a hundred thousand, we could west merge with strong Qin and north resist Great Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Victory would yield territory to face Qin and Wei.

sentences.zh: 夫欲拓境開疆，保寧社稷，無過今也。

translations.literal: For desiring to widen territory and open frontiers, guarding altars of soil and grain, nothing surpasses now.
translations.idiomatic: No better moment existed to enlarge the realm.

sentences.zh: 如使後機失會，豪桀復起，梟除桓玄，布惟新之化，遐邇既寧，物無異望，非但建鄴難屠，江北亦不可冀。

translations.literal: If afterward the opportunity slips and heroes rise again, when Huan Xuan is cut off and only fresh reform spreads, far and near already calm and things without other hope, not only Jiankang will be hard to butcher, the north of the river also cannot be hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Delay would let Jin recover and close the window.

sentences.zh: 機過患生，憂必至矣。

translations.literal: When the opportunity passes, calamity arises; worry is sure to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Miss the moment and trouble would follow.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，悔將及焉。

translations.literal: Heaven gives and we do not take; regret will reach us.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven-sent chances wasted bring regret.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下覽之。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty consider it.'
translations.idiomatic: He begged Murong De to act.

sentences.zh: 」德曰：「自頃數纏百六，宏綱暫弛，遂令奸逆亂華，舊京墟穢，每尋否運，憤慨兼懷。

translations.literal: De said, 'Recently fate has repeatedly tangled in misfortune, the great net hung slack, letting treacherous rebels disorder the Hua heartland and the old capital lie in filth; each time I ponder this ill fortune, indignation fills my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De answered that he nursed a long grudge against the barbarians who ruined Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 昔少康以一旅之眾，復夏配天，況朕據三齊之地，藉五州之眾，教之以軍旅，訓之以禮讓，上下知義，人思自奮，繕甲待釁，為日久矣。

translations.literal: Formerly Shaokang with one brigade's host restored Xia and matched Heaven; how much more I occupy the land of the three Qi, rely on the hosts of five provinces, teach them with armies, train them with ritual yielding; above and below know righteousness, each man thinks to rouse himself; we repair armor and await a crack—this has been long.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Shaokang and boasted his Shandong base and trained army.

sentences.zh: 但欲先定中原，掃除逋孽，然後宣佈淳風，經理九服，飲馬長江，懸旌隴阪。

translations.literal: But I wish first to settle the central plain, sweep away fleeing villains, then spread pure wind, order the nine domains, drink horses at the Yangzi, hang banners on the Long slopes.
translations.idiomatic: He still meant to pacify the north before marching south.

sentences.zh: 此志未遂，且韜戈耳。

translations.literal: This intent is not yet fulfilled; for now we sheathe the spears only.
translations.idiomatic: His southern strike remained deferred.

sentences.zh: 今者之事，王公其詳議之。

translations.literal: As for today's matter, let the royal dukes deliberate in detail.'
translations.idiomatic: He asked his nobles to debate Han Fan's plan.

sentences.zh: 」咸以桓玄新得志，未可圖，乃止。

translations.literal: All thought Huan Xuan newly triumphant and not yet to be plotted against, and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Huan Xuan too strong for the moment and dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 於是講武於城西，步兵三十七萬，車一萬七千乘，鐵騎五萬三千，周亙山澤，旌旗彌漫，鉦鼓之聲，振動天地。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drilled troops west of the city: three hundred seventy thousand foot, seventeen thousand carts, fifty-three thousand armored horse, filling mountains and marshes, banners covering heaven, the clash of gongs and drums shaking heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: He staged a review west of the city with hundreds of thousands on parade.

sentences.zh: 德登高望之，顧謂劉軌、高雅之曰：「昔郤克仇齊，子胥怨楚，終能暢其剛烈，名流千載。

translations.literal: De climbed high and looked over them, and said to Liu Gui and Gao Yazhi, 'Formerly Xi Ke avenged Qi, Wu Zixu resented Chu, and in the end they could vent their fierce integrity and their names flow a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: He flattered the Jin defectors as avengers like Xi Ke and Wu Zixu.

sentences.zh: 卿等既知投身有道，當使無慚昔人也。

translations.literal: You gentlemen already know to cast yourselves onto a rightful way; you should make yourselves not ashamed before the ancients.'
translations.idiomatic: He urged them to live up to those models.

sentences.zh: 」雅之等頓首答曰：「幸蒙陛下天覆之恩，大造之澤，存亡繼絕，實在聖時，雖則萬隕，何以上報！

translations.literal: Yazhi and others knocked their heads and replied, 'We have received Your Majesty's heaven-covering grace and great creation's moisture, preserving the dying and continuing the cut off—truly in this sage season; though we shattered ten thousand times, how repay on high!'
translations.idiomatic: They swore loyalty in return.

sentences.zh: 」俄聞桓玄敗，德以慕容鎮為前鋒，慕容鐘為大都督，配以步卒二萬，騎五千，克期將發，而德寢疾，於是罷兵。

translations.literal: Soon they heard Huan Xuan was defeated; De made Murong Zhen vanguard and Murong Zhong supreme commander, pairing them with twenty thousand foot and five thousand horse, fixing a date to set out, but De took to bed ill, and therefore the army was halted.
translations.idiomatic: When news came of Huan Xuan's fall Murong De mobilized then canceled the campaign because of illness.

sentences.zh: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。

translations.literal: Earlier, De had welcomed his brother's son Chao from Chang'an; at this point he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao, whom he had summoned from Chang'an, now arrived.

sentences.zh: 德夜夢其父曰：「汝既無子，何不早立超為太子，不爾，惡人生心。

translations.literal: De dreamed at night his father said, 'You have no son; why not early establish Chao as crown prince—otherwise evil men will breed designs.'
translations.idiomatic: Murong De dreamed his father told him to adopt Murong Chao as heir.

sentences.zh: 」寐而告其妻曰：「先帝神明所敕，觀此夢意，吾將死矣。

translations.literal: Awake he told his wife, 'The late emperor's spirit commanded; looking at this dream's meaning, I am about to die.'
translations.idiomatic: He told his consort the dream foretold his death.

sentences.zh: 」乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict making Chao crown prince, amnestied the realm, and for sons continuing fathers raised each man's rank two grades.
translations.idiomatic: He named Murong Chao crown prince and issued a broad amnesty.

sentences.zh: 其月死，即也，時年七十。

translations.literal: That month he died, passing from the world; at the time his age was seventy sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same month at seventy sui.

sentences.zh: 乃夜為十餘棺，分出四門，潛葬山谷，竟不知其屍之所在。

translations.literal: That night they made more than ten coffins, sent them out the four gates separately, and secretly buried him in mountain valleys; in the end none knew where his corpse lay.
translations.idiomatic: They ran decoy coffers out each gate and hid his true burial in the hills.

sentences.zh: 在位五年。

translations.literal: He held the throne five years.
translations.idiomatic: His reign lasted five years.

sentences.zh: 偽諡獻武皇帝。

translations.literal: He was posthumously titled Emperor Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: His temple posthumous title was Emperor Xianwu.
